doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Pay from Rollins and life lessons
summary: He never asked about money; when a world tour was canceled Rollins paid him anyway. The life lessons were not to mess up on the gig.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well speaking of taking care of business, I mean this may sound like an “of course not” question but would it occur to you at that moment where Sonny said “Okay you got the gig” do you — at what point do you ask about money?

Okay. Well you know what I never asked about money. Because I just always figured it would be okay. And you know it was okay. And look Sonny at one point you know he was going to go out and do a world tour. And we rehearsed one time and then it all got canceled. And that was that last time he played, and that was the last time I played with him. But you know what? He paid me for the missing — he paid me a good amount of money to — you missed the gig, it was canceled, here’s the money. He’s a mensch.
Yeah ‘cause you had set aside those dates and probably turned down other work.
And did that. But you know when he called you had to be there you know. That was it. You know and so there was no question about that.
Have you had people, maybe Sonny Rollins, other people that taught you life lessons as well as musical lessons?
Well the life lessons were don’t mess up. You know don’t get drunk on the gig or whatever. Just yeah, I mean just do what you do and do it the best you can do it.
